name: Photoelastic polariscope
summary: Stress made visible: a screen, one polariser sheet and a phone. The cheapest first real-world build. On paper.

assumptions.assumption: the screen's light is linearly polarised
assumptions.how_checked: rotate the analyser sheet over the white screen: near-black at one angle
assumptions.if_broken: no fringes; use a second sheet as the polariser
assumptions.door: put a second polariser sheet over a plain light source

assumptions.assumption: the part is linear elastic and its fringes do not creep in time
assumptions.how_checked: photograph at 10 s and 5 min under a fixed load; fringe order unchanged within 0.1
assumptions.if_broken: photoviscoelastic: report time under load with every reading
assumptions.door: report the time under load with every reading (photoviscoelastic)

assumptions.assumption: residual (frozen-in) stress is known or subtracted
assumptions.how_checked: photograph the unloaded part first; that image is the zero
assumptions.if_broken: the moulding stresses of the Brockhaus figures, exactly; subtract the zero image
assumptions.door: photograph the unloaded part and subtract that zero image

assumptions.assumption: stress is uniform through the thickness (plane stress)
assumptions.how_checked: thin flat parts only; thickness under a tenth of the in-plane size
assumptions.if_broken: an integrated value, not a local one

assumptions.assumption: the colour-to-order map holds for this screen and camera
assumptions.how_checked: the stage-2 twin's map against the calibration disc, order by order
assumptions.if_broken: count orders in single-colour light instead
assumptions.door: count orders in single-colour light instead
